Past analyses of AAPL (most recent first):

[2026-08-26 | AAPL | Overweight | +3.7% | +3.8% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: Overweight AAPL at $313.45 — constructive direction, but staged and gated rather than bought at spot. Take only a 10–15 bps starter (half or less of the plan's 25–50 bps tranche one) via limit inside the 309.11–311.22 confluence (VWMA 309.11 / Bollinger mid 310.26 / 50-SMA 311.22), sized off 2×ATR (~14.4 pts) instead of the 5-point stop distance, with 306.00 as the hard risk line and 308.80 as the reduce line; do not chase above 315. Add tranche two (25–50 bps) only on a daily close above 320.28 with volume >55M (half size at 45–55M) and tranche three (25–50 bps) only on a close above 323.40 with a held retest of 320.28, capping total exposure at 125–150 bps of portfolio and total position risk at 0.25–0.50%. Trim one-third at 327.74, one-third at 333.43, trail the remainder toward 340.08–344.57, lift the stop to breakeven after the first target; horizon 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October FQ4 FY26 print.

**Investment Thesis**: DIRECTION IS SETTLED BY THE FUNDAMENTALS; ONLY THE ENTRY IS CONTESTED — hence Overweight, not Buy.

The bull side wins the business question essentially unopposed. 9M FY26 revenue +16.1%, net income +20.0%, diluted EPS +22.4%, gross margin 50.06%; Q3 revenue $109.42B +16.4% with COGS up only 8.6% and operating margin 32.62%; gross-profit growth accelerated three straight quarters (+18.8% → +22.1% → +25.3%); normalized FCF +37.5% with $62.17B of net cash, debt retired, current ratio above 1.0x, and receivables down 21.1% while revenue rose. None of the bear material is deterioration — it is extrapolation risk.

The conservative analyst's caveats are legitimate and must be carried as risk controls, not dismissed: the ~$10.8B cash-tax timing benefit reverses (headline CFO +43.1% overstates the 37.5% run-rate); memory inflation of 80–180 bps would take gross margin to roughly 48.3–49.3% and is an inference from an NVDA AI-server headline, not an Apple disclosure; the $13.3B gross intangible with no matching acquisition outflow and the $13.5B noncurrent-liability rise remain unexplained; inventory +94% with raw materials +260% against finished goods −4%; R&D +32.5% for three quarters caps operating leverage; buybacks down 12% YoY; and ~35x trailing / low-30s forward with a ~3% FCF yield is not cheap. But no reported data yet shows margin decay, so these are gates on size and confirmation, not a sell signal.

On the tape the bull owns the primary trend and the bear owns the entry. AAPL at 313.45 is 11.1% above a rising 200-SMA at 282.12; the 50-SMA has re-inflected upward six straight sessions to 311.22; the 10-EMA has curled to 310.85; the MACD histogram just printed +0.1517, its first positive reading in 18 sessions, with the line up from −2.676 to −1.10; Bollinger bandwidth has collapsed 22.6% → 8.46%, the narrowest in the window, with %B at 62.1; RSI 51.43 is neither overbought nor broken. Against that: today's 34.0M shares is 68% of the ~49.9M 20-day average, the five-session average is ~36.5M, the 8/20 down day (41.0M) and 8/21 down day (46.9M) were heavier than today's up day, and 320.28 rejected once, closing 2.79% off the high. A squeeze at 8.46% bandwidth tells you resolution is coming, not which way.

The decisive arithmetic — and the reason the aggressive analyst's full-size tranche one is rejected — is the stop inconsistency he never rebutted. ATR is 7.19 (2.29% of price). A 306 stop from 311 is 5 points, ~0.70 ATR, i.e. inside normal daily noise, while the plan itself requires that 2×ATR (~14.4 points) never exceed the intended per-position loss. And AAPL gapped −7.36% on 132.5M shares on 2026-07-31, roughly twice the stop distance; size set by 5 points is only safe in a world without gaps. A 25–50 bps tranche at 311 therefore risks materially more than the advertised 1.6%, ahead of two explicit, unhedgeable binaries (NVDA earnings, the inflation print). The fix is not the conservative analyst's prohibition — that is an overcorrection: if AAPL gaps through 320.28 the "wait for everything" plan either misses the move or chases it at a worse reward-to-risk, and my own AAPL record is unambiguous that fighting a rising 200-SMA on a fortress balance sheet is the losing side of the coin flip (the 07-13, 07-20, 07-21, 07-22 and 08-12 Underweights each forfeited 3–5% of five-day alpha by trimming momentum decay inside an intact uptrend, and the 08-17 and 08-13 Underweights at support added −2.7% and −3.9% alpha against the call). The fix is a small, conditional starter sized off 2ATR, with the full ladder reserved for confirmation.

Why not Hold, and why not Underweight. The bear's pricing claim is unevidenced on the supplied data — there are no consensus multiples, no guidance, no revision series — and he explicitly frames a risk-management problem, not a deterioration thesis; his own material states the business is not broken. Hold would also misprice the skew: downside is bounded by a small gap-sized starter and a defined 306 line, while a close above 323.40 opens 327.74, then 333.43, then 340.08–344.57. Underweight is contradicted by the last two weeks of this name's own outcomes, which penalized exactly this trim-at-support pattern.

Execution adopted: the neutral construction, with the conservative analyst's gap arithmetic bolted on. Tranche one 10–15 bps (not 25–50) only inside 309.11–311.22 and only on a defended retest or a close back above 311.22 on better volume (~45M+); the pre-event starter may be skipped entirely if the caller cannot absorb gap risk, but then the tranche-two gate must not be chased. Tranche two 25–50 bps on a daily close above 320.28 with >55M (half size at 45–55M); tranche three 25–50 bps above 323.40 with a held retest of 320.28; 125–150 bps cap only after both volume confirmation and gross-margin durability evidence. Reduce on two consecutive closes below 308.80; move to Underweight on a close below 300.00. The prior 2026-08-19 lesson applies directly: the entry trigger then sat only ~0.8% above spot and the five-day window (−1.1% raw, −0.7% alpha) tested only the starter, not the thesis — so the add conditions here are pre-committed and priced, and the review is at the FQ4 print, not at day five.

What would change the call. Upgrade to Buy on a daily close above 323.40 that holds a retest of 320.28 on >55M shares, or on FQ4 gross margin ≥49.5% with inventory flat-to-down and the evidence gaps filled. Cut back toward Hold if Q4 FY26 gross margin falls below 48%, if COGS growth exceeds revenue growth for two consecutive quarters, if the FY26 10-K does not explain the $13.3B intangible, or if memory-cost guidance is materially worse than the 80–180 bps range. Go to Underweight on a close below 300.00. Stated gaps, not papered over: no segment or geographic revenue split (so 50.06% margin durability is unattributable), no consensus/valuation cross-check, no guidance, no options or implied-vol data (so a protective collar for the October window cannot be priced here), no news window resolution for the 07-31 gap, and no portfolio context — so all sizing is expressed as a fraction of the caller's own standard AAPL allocation (100 bps) and must respect their single-name and mega-cap concentration caps, and every target here is technical rather than valuation-derived.

**Price Target**: 327.74

**Time Horizon**: 1-3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October FQ4 FY26 print and FY26 10-K

REFLECTION:
The five-day window returned +3.7% raw and +3.8% alpha versus SPY, so the Overweight direction was right, but this is too short to judge a 1–3 month thesis whose first real test is the late-October FQ4 print. What it does support is the core claim that the primary trend and fortress balance sheet dominate — and it quietly undercuts my own execution, since a starter gated at 309.11–311.22 sat 1–2% below a 313.45 spot and likely never filled, repeating the 08-19 error of pricing the entry below a rising tape. Lesson for next time: when the trend and fundamentals already agree, take the ATR-sized starter at or near spot and express the caution in size, not in a pullback limit that the direction call itself argues against.

[2026-08-25 | AAPL | Hold | +4.9% | +5.5% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Hold

**Executive Summary**: Hold AAPL at standard/benchmark weight at 309.90: do not add inside the 300.00–320.28 coil, and trim only any excess above target — the range, not the franchise, is the problem. The only add is conditional: a daily close above 320.28 on >50M shares with MACD above zero, sized at no more than 1/6 to 1/3 of intended incremental exposure, initial stop near 310 (just under the 50-SMA 310.88 / VWMA 309.19 confluence, ~1.4×ATR) then trailed at roughly 1.5 ATR, with a second tranche released only by a Q4 FY26 gross-margin guide ≥49.5% and revenue growth ≥12%. Risk control: a daily close below 300.00 on expanding volume cuts 1/3 to 1/2 of the position (293.39, then 281.90 as next references), and the core must be sized so a repeat of the 7/31 gap straight to 293–282 does not breach the caller's risk budget. Horizon 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the Q4 FY26 print and FY26 10-K.

**Investment Thesis**: The three seats agree on the facts and disagree only on what to do with an unresolved coil; after weighing them, the neutral construction survives and the rating is Hold, not a fence-sit.

Why the aggressive seat does not get the add. It is right that 309.90 against a 50 SMA of 310.88 is a 0.31% undershoot and that calling that a breakdown is overheated — that point stands. But "small" is not "meaningless." AAPL is simultaneously below the 50 SMA, the 10 EMA (310.27), the Bollinger middle (311.50) and the VWMA (309.19) — a four-way confluence compressed into ~2.3 points with %B at 0.456 and ATR at 7.23 (27% compressed) — while MACD and its signal are both below zero, the histogram repair has decelerated (−3.63 to −0.15 over nine sessions), and volume has faded three straight sessions into 8/25's 25.87M. That is the definition of unconfirmed, and unconfirmed is not a loaded spring. Its 316.83 pilot add is the tell: it needs a MACD cross above the signal line but not above zero and buys straight into the 313–320 supply cluster, front-running the plan's own confirmation stack — rejected. Its $378 buyback anchor is derived from 164.3M net shares retired, so the actual average repurchase price is at or below that figure; it is a soft statement of management's view of value, not a floor that defends 309.90. And its 7/31 causal story — that the gap repriced the Q3 10-Q — collides with the timeline: the filing was accepted 14:01 UTC (10:01 ET) while the gap printed at the open from 333.43 to 304.81 with a 300.00 low. The aggressive restated the hypothesis rather than answering the timestamp; an unattributed −7.35% gap on 132.5M shares is a reason for humility, not a base to underwrite.

Why the conservative seat does not get the veto. It wins the two points that matter for sizing: 300.00 is gap-able (293.39 and 281.90 are the real downstream references), so a "3.2% to the stop" framing is fiction and the position must be sized for a gap, not a smooth stop; and adding one-third with a fixed 310 stop inside compressed ATR is too generous if volatility expands post-breakout. But it over-applies the lesson in both directions. Demanding two consecutive closes above 320.28 on >50M shares, in a coil whose bandwidth has compressed from 18.9% to 11.6%, is over-insurance that all but guarantees missing a gap-through resolution. And 302.94 as a cut trigger is inside the noise of a 302–317 box whose lower Bollinger sits near 293 — that is a whipsaw level, not a structural one. The correct conservative contribution is tail-survivability sizing, not refusal to add on confirmation.

What decided it. The neutral seat's reading holds up under both critiques: the coil is genuinely two-sided, so benchmark weight is right, the 320.28/50M/MACD-above-zero stack is kept, the 316.83 pilot is rejected, the first tranche is staged down to 1/6–1/3 with the balance pending a second confirmation close or a clean hold of 316–318, the stop trails at ~1.5 ATR once through the trigger, and the structural invalidation stays at 300.00 on expanding volume. Fundamentals forbid a Sell or Underweight: Q3 revenue +16.4%, gross margin 50.06% (+357bp), EPS +28.7%, 9M FCF $110.2B (+52.5%), net cash $62.2B with no new long-term issuance, current ratio above 1.0 for the first time, the 300.00 gap floor intact 17 sessions, and price 9.93% above a rising 200 SMA at 281.90 with the 50 over the 200. Forward risks forbid a Buy: the 50.06% margin is backward-looking against raw materials +260% to $7.6B and total inventory +94% (a pre-build or a write-down candidate, not provably a hedge), deferred revenue +4.3% versus revenue +16% undercuts the durable-Services-margin claim, the tax rate has already moved 15.39% → 17.58%, roughly $15–16B of the 9M operating-cash-flow beat looks like working-capital timing, buybacks slowed 12% while net intangibles jumped 91% with no new term debt (a capital-allocation/M&A pivot, two-sided), and 34x trailing / ~2.8% clean FCF yield is not a margin-of-safety valuation. Buying at 309.90 means paying up in the middle of the coil where the plan's own math gives thin reward-to-risk to 329.61.

Prior outcomes bind both ways. The 08-11 Underweight (+2.1% alpha) and the 07-20–07-24 Underweight string (−3.2% to −3.8%) failed by acting on fading volume inside a rising long-term trend; the 08-12/08-13 Underweights (+5.3%, +3.9% alpha) failed for trimming on momentum decay without a confirmed close below support. That is why there is no pre-emptive trim here. The 08-14 Overweight earned +2.5% alpha directionally but its 10%/10% gating left most of the intended size undeployed — hence stage the add rather than refuse it, and size the first tranche at 1/6–1/3 rather than nothing.

What would change it. Upgrade to Overweight only when all three print: a daily close above 320.28 on >50M shares, MACD above zero, and a Q4 gross-margin guide ≥49.5% with revenue growth ≥12%. Downgrade to Underweight on a daily close below 300.00 on expanding volume (1/3 to 1/2 reduction, 293.39 then 281.90), or on a gross-margin guide disappointment; move toward Sell on a high-volume break of 293.39 or a guide ≤47.5% with revenue decelerating below 10%. Stated gaps, not papered over: no segment, geographic or unit-volume data, so 50.06% gross-margin durability is unattributable; the 7/31 gap cause is unresolved; no options chain or implied-vol data, so a protective put/collar cannot be priced; no consensus forward EPS to cross-check the ~34x multiple; and no portfolio context, so all sizing is expressed as fractions of the caller's own standard AAPL weight and 320.28/329.61/333.43 are technical levels, not valuation-derived targets.

**Price Target**: 320.28

**Time Horizon**: 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the Q4 FY26 print and FY26 10-K

REFLECTION:
The +5.5% five-day alpha versus SPY shows the Hold was directionally too cautious—the stock rose +4.9%—though five days is too short to validate the 1–3 month coil thesis. That undercuts the “unconfirmed is not a loaded spring” premise and the refusal to add below 320.28, while supporting the no-pre-emptive-trim call and the 300.00 structural floor. Next time, use a time-boxed starter position or loosen the volume condition on the 320.28 close trigger so a gap-through resolution is not forfeited by an over-strict confirmation stack.

[2026-08-24 | AAPL | Underweight | +2.1% | +1.6% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Underweight AAPL at 310.34: sell roughly 40–45% of your current AAPL exposure at the verified close and keep the residual 55–60% as a core. Do not ladder the reduction to a rally — complete it now — but size the residual so a mark-to-market at 281.70 (the rising 200-SMA) is a loss you have pre-agreed you can absorb; if it isn't, trim more. Treat 316.83 as a warning line, not an automatic re-add (the trader's plan had the same level as both a second sale and a full restore, which is a whipsaw rule into an event week); a volume close above 320.28 is the cleaner partial restore to standard weight. Downside: alert at 307.01, volume-confirmed action below 305.74 takes you to 40–45% of standard, a daily close below 300.57 on expanding volume cuts to 25–30% of standard, with 290.88 then 281.70 as downstream references. Horizon 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October FQ4 FY26 gross-margin print.

**Investment Thesis**: All three risk seats converged on reducing AAPL and none defended full size — aggressive for a midpoint trim, conservative for the larger end of the band, neutral for 40–45% — so the direction is not the question. The rating question is degree, and the honest answer is the middle of the three: act, but do not over-trim, because the record on this name says five-day alpha has repeatedly gone against Underweights.

The reduce case wins on three unrebutted points. First, arithmetic: at 310.34 with a structural stop at 300.57–300.00 and the first honest target the 50% retrace at 320.04, the leg is ~0.94:1, and the downside scenario is worse than modelled because the 07-31 session ranged 300.00–333.43 on 132.5M shares — documented proof that a close-based stop can fill five to ten points below the trigger.
